correctness.rationale: In A=k[x_1..x_n]/(x_i x_j,i≠j;x_i^3), nilpotence forces endomorphism generator images into maximal ideal, with linear P and quadratic Q. Distinct generator relations force row-sparsity; idempotence F²=F forces P²=P, R=P^[2] projection and Q=QP+RQ. Every nonzero row of row-sparse idempotent P points to a unique identity root, and all other rows independently choose zero or scalar multiple of a root row. If r roots, P and R have rank r, admissible Q consists of two free off-diagonal projection blocks, dimension 2r(n−r) for any characteristic (including 2). Image is isomorphic to A_{r,3}, rank 1+2r. Number binom(n,r)(1+r(q−1))^(n−r) q^(2r(n−r)). Independent integer calculation for n2,q3 yields [1,54,1]; n3,q2 [1,192,144,1]; n4,q2 [1,2048,13824,1024,1]. Exact finite checks corroborate the all-field proof; source checker.py read fully.

originality.rationale: The already published exact automorphism normal form for the same truncated coordinate-cross algebras covers invertible maps only (r=n). Epstein–Nguyen prove graded retract structural results for Stanley–Reisner rings and certain monomial quotients, but do not enumerate all possibly nongraded composition-idempotent maps of this cubically truncated Artinian ring. Díaz et al treat characteristic-zero automorphism groups, not the finite-field entire retraction monoid. The intermediate-rank polynomial and char-independent Q-block freedom are not consequences of an automorphism count.

The literature comparison is best-of-knowledge; an older unindexed explicit retraction monoid census remains possible.

value.rationale: A_{n,3} is a canonical first nontrivial truncated union-of-axes fiber product with nilpotent quadratic data. The theorem simultaneously classifies all image isomorphism types and gives every finite-field map-count by natural rank, including genuinely nongraded retracts and characteristic-two behavior. This fills a meaningful enumerative gap rather than recomputing automorphism sizes.

scientific_limitations: Counts labeled unital maps, not conjugacy classes, distinct images, nongraded isomorphisms or branch lengths d>3.
Finite checks do not replace the arbitrary-field structural proof.
